bull_bear.body:
- Diversified product portfolio spanning Pharmaceuticals, Agro intermediates, Dyes, Perfumery and Paint intermediates, catering to a wide range of industrial applications
- Proven ability to maintain market share and margins in Agro-intermediates despite new competitive capacity additions in the Chloro-Toluene segment
- Established export relationships positioning the Company to benefit from the shift in global supply chains away from single-country sourcing
- Debt-free balance sheet following retirement of all outstanding debt during the year, giving financial flexibility and a lower cost base
- Availability of skilled technical manpower and improving manufacturing capability, supported by ongoing investment in training and technology upgradation
- Circular process design: waste streams treated and recovered, with recovered materials either reused as process inputs or sold as value-added products, contributing to input cost reduction
- Active R&D programme and structured market studies aimed at diversifying the product range and reducing segment concentration
- Increasing focus on specialty chemicals and value-added products
- SAP implemented, improving data flow and accuracy particularly in accounts and finance
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Low-cost Chinese import competition suppressing realisations — Management states intense competition from low-cost Chinese manufacturers continues to suppress realisations in several product segments. During 2025-26 it drove demand shrinkage in PG and derivatives and contract-manufacturing products, and prevented a sharp rise in raw material prices from being passed on in PHPG derivatives, compressing margins in the last two quarters.
- Raw material price volatility and dependence on imported feedstock — The Company flags high dependence on imported raw materials and feedstock for certain chemical products, exposing it to global supply chain disruptions and currency fluctuations; volatility in raw material prices and forex directly impacted margins, as experienced with PHPG derivatives during the year.
- Product and segment concentration in commodity-priced intermediates — The declared aim of the R&D programme and market studies is to derisk the portfolio by diversifying the product range, reducing segment concentration and developing intermediates less exposed to commodity pricing cycles and import substitution pressures - an explicit acknowledgement that the current mix is concentrated and commodity-exposed. Conventional PG derivatives are described as of declining relevance.
- Energy intensity of operations — Operations are energy-intensive, leaving results sensitive to changes in fuel, power and logistics costs.
- Environmental, health and safety regulation and changing compliance requirements — Stringent EHS regulation requires continuous investment in compliance and sustainability measures, and changes in environmental laws, regulatory frameworks and compliance requirements are flagged as leading to increased operational costs.
- Geopolitical uncertainty, trade restrictions and global slowdown affecting exports — Flagged as affecting demand and exports and as necessitating more active short- and medium-term strategic planning; the global socio-economic environment is described as remaining in turmoil with trade fragmentation and sustained supply chain disruption, and near-term demand is expected to remain measured.
- Execution and gestation risk on expansion and R&D — Long gestation periods and high capital expenditure requirements are cited for R&D and for setting up and expanding manufacturing facilities, while several projects - the Cephalexin enzymatic-route intermediate, agro/pharma capacity expansions, de-bottlenecking and the wastewater recycling plant - remain in progress; the year's investments have already weighed on reported profitability in the short term.
- Regulatory and administrative complexity from the corporate restructuring — Flagged explicitly: the demerger-related company name change disrupted export registrations, with foreign buyers requiring time to re-register new vendor details, which disrupted export activity in the final quarter.
- Climate change, resource availability and stakeholder sustainability expectations — Listed by the Company as a threat, alongside technological disruption and changing customer preferences requiring continuous innovation and adaptation.

outlook.body:
- Use the period of subdued demand as a strategic window to invest in the business rather than defend the status quo - directing capital expenditure at enhancement and upgradation of existing equipment and production systems.
- Eliminate inefficiencies through internal operational reviews, renegotiated procurement frameworks, streamlined supply chain processes and rationalised cost structures across the organisation.
- Execute a structured programme of investment and innovation to strengthen existing operations and broaden the product base.
- Enter the pharmaceutical green chemistry space with an enzymatic synthesis route intermediate for Cephalexin, directly addressing the declining relevance of conventional PG derivatives.
- De-risk the portfolio through an active R&D programme and structured market studies - diversifying the product range, reducing segment concentration and developing intermediates less exposed to commodity pricing cycles and import substitution pressures.
- Diversify into alternative usage markets such as Dyes, Brighteners and Fragrances to compensate for weaker Pharma demand.
- Operate a formalised, more active Board framework for short- and medium-term strategic review to optimise outcomes and manage emerging risks.
- Pursue independent growth strategies and specialized collaborations as a standalone chemicals entity following the NCLT-sanctioned demerger effective 17 December 2025.
- Maintain a debt-free balance sheet as the foundation for funding growth opportunities.
- Manage macroeconomic and sectoral pressure by optimizing cost structures through alternative sourcing, engaging closely with global customers and maintaining operational efficiencies.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During 2025-26 the Company deliberately used a period of subdued demand as a window to invest, directing capital expenditure toward the enhancement and upgradation of existing equipment and production systems; management notes these investments weighed on reported profitability in the short term but were considered essential to position the business operationally, structurally and competitively for recovering markets. Looking ahead, the Company is executing a structured programme of investment and innovation. The flagship project is a next-generation pharmaceutical intermediate enabling an enzymatic - rather than conventional chemical - synthesis route for Cephalexin production, being commissioned in an existing facility and expected to be operational by year end; it is the Company's second product in the pharmaceutical green chemistry space and is intended to address the declining relevance of conventional PG derivatives. Alongside it, capacity expansions across selected Agro and pharma intermediates, targeted de-bottlenecking, and the installation of a wastewater recycling plant are in various stages of progress. The recycling plant, currently under installation, will recover a large volume of water from a major process effluent stream for reuse in production processes and cooling systems, reducing both water drawn from outside and the volume requiring treatment and disposal. R&D is underway to push recovery rates further from multiple streams. The Company also cites scope for capacity expansion and strategic partnerships, and notes that the retirement of all outstanding debt during the year leaves it debt-free with improved capacity to invest in growth. Structurally, the NCLT-sanctioned Scheme demerged the Chemical Undertaking (including Daurala Organics and Daurala Chemical Industries) into the Company effective 17 December 2025, and the disposal of Dahej Land is noted as a material development after the year end. No rupee quantum for any of these projects is disclosed in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Agro-intermediate business showed a meaningful revival, with customer pipeline stocks beginning to clear after nearly two years of stagnation; market conditions are expected to remain robust in the year ahead.
- Demand shrinkage in PG and derivatives and contract manufacturing products, driven by lower demand for the final APIs and the impact of cheaper Chinese imports.
- PHPG derivatives margins came under significant pressure in the last two quarters after a sharp rise in raw material prices that could not be passed on due to intense Chinese import competition and geo-political conditions.
- Export activity in the final quarter was disrupted by the company name change following the demerger, with foreign buyers requiring time to re-register new vendor details.
- Near-term demand is expected to remain measured, with the Company positioned to benefit from a gradual recovery in end-market demand as macroeconomic conditions eventually stabilize.
- Strong domestic demand driven by early-stage resurgence in end-user industries such as Dyes, Brighteners and Agro-chem.
- The new Cephalexin green-chemistry intermediate is anticipated to reinvigorate a declining product line with both domestic and export customers.
- Shift in global supply chains away from single-country sourcing creating an opportunity for India as a preferred manufacturing hub, with the Company well positioned given its established export relationships.
- Expansion in downstream industries such as water treatment, renewable energy, electronics and construction expected to support future demand for the product range.
- Currency risk is largely naturally hedged - annual fixation of export product prices and imported input costs mitigates foreign exchange risk to a large extent, despite the Rupee depreciating 4.98% against the US Dollar during the second half of 2025.
- Investments made during the year have weighed on reported profitability in the short term, but the Board regards them as essential to capture the benefits of recovering markets.
- Customer pipeline stocks in the Agro-intermediate business are beginning to clear after nearly two years of stagnation, with market conditions expected to remain robust in the year ahead.

moat.body:
- Diversified product portfolio spanning Pharmaceuticals, Agro intermediates, Dyes, Perfumery and Paint intermediates, catering to a wide range of industrial applications
- Proven ability to maintain market share and margins in Agro-intermediates despite new competitive capacity additions in the Chloro-Toluene segment
- Established export relationships positioning the Company to benefit from the shift in global supply chains away from single-country sourcing
- Debt-free balance sheet following retirement of all outstanding debt during the year, giving financial flexibility and a lower cost base
- Availability of skilled technical manpower and improving manufacturing capability, supported by ongoing investment in training and technology upgradation
- Circular process design: waste streams treated and recovered, with recovered materials either reused as process inputs or sold as value-added products, contributing to input cost reduction
- Active R&D programme and structured market studies aimed at diversifying the product range and reducing segment concentration
- Increasing focus on specialty chemicals and value-added products
- SAP implemented, improving data flow and accuracy particularly in accounts and finance

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Low-cost Chinese import competition suppressing realisations — Management states intense competition from low-cost Chinese manufacturers continues to suppress realisations in several product segments. During 2025-26 it drove demand shrinkage in PG and derivatives and contract-manufacturing products, and prevented a sharp rise in raw material prices from being passed on in PHPG derivatives, compressing margins in the last two quarters.
- Raw material price volatility and dependence on imported feedstock — The Company flags high dependence on imported raw materials and feedstock for certain chemical products, exposing it to global supply chain disruptions and currency fluctuations; volatility in raw material prices and forex directly impacted margins, as experienced with PHPG derivatives during the year.
- Product and segment concentration in commodity-priced intermediates — The declared aim of the R&D programme and market studies is to derisk the portfolio by diversifying the product range, reducing segment concentration and developing intermediates less exposed to commodity pricing cycles and import substitution pressures - an explicit acknowledgement that the current mix is concentrated and commodity-exposed. Conventional PG derivatives are described as of declining relevance.
- Energy intensity of operations — Operations are energy-intensive, leaving results sensitive to changes in fuel, power and logistics costs.
- Environmental, health and safety regulation and changing compliance requirements — Stringent EHS regulation requires continuous investment in compliance and sustainability measures, and changes in environmental laws, regulatory frameworks and compliance requirements are flagged as leading to increased operational costs.
- Geopolitical uncertainty, trade restrictions and global slowdown affecting exports — Flagged as affecting demand and exports and as necessitating more active short- and medium-term strategic planning; the global socio-economic environment is described as remaining in turmoil with trade fragmentation and sustained supply chain disruption, and near-term demand is expected to remain measured.
- Execution and gestation risk on expansion and R&D — Long gestation periods and high capital expenditure requirements are cited for R&D and for setting up and expanding manufacturing facilities, while several projects - the Cephalexin enzymatic-route intermediate, agro/pharma capacity expansions, de-bottlenecking and the wastewater recycling plant - remain in progress; the year's investments have already weighed on reported profitability in the short term.
- Regulatory and administrative complexity from the corporate restructuring — Flagged explicitly: the demerger-related company name change disrupted export registrations, with foreign buyers requiring time to re-register new vendor details, which disrupted export activity in the final quarter.
- Climate change, resource availability and stakeholder sustainability expectations — Listed by the Company as a threat, alongside technological disruption and changing customer preferences requiring continuous innovation and adaptation.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Use the period of subdued demand as a strategic window to invest in the business rather than defend the status quo - directing capital expenditure at enhancement and upgradation of existing equipment and production systems.
- Eliminate inefficiencies through internal operational reviews, renegotiated procurement frameworks, streamlined supply chain processes and rationalised cost structures across the organisation.
- Execute a structured programme of investment and innovation to strengthen existing operations and broaden the product base.

hero.oneLiner: DCM Shriram Fine Chemicals is a manufacturer of chemical intermediates for the pharmaceutical, agro-chemical, optical brightener, dye, perfumery and paint industries, which became an independent listed entity when the Chemical Undertaking was demerged into it effective 17 December 2025.
